brief: BTIG's technical strategy note argues last week's correlated selling pushed SPX near its 200 DMA and produced the first 80% NYSE downside volume day in nearly a year, but these are necessary, not sufficient, conditions for a bottom. After such a setup historically, forward 20-50 day returns are close to a coin toss (11 of 15 prior cases since 1996 saw another 80% day within 30 days; SPX was higher only 53% of the time 20 days out, averaging +0.31%). A real 'fat pitch' needs SPX closer to 7,000-7,100 with a deeper breadth washout: only 58% of SPX names are above their 200 DMA now versus under 30% at a durable bottom, and put/call ratios remain well below March/July lows. SOX broke its 200 DMA for the first time since May 2025, which BTIG reads as another coin toss near-term but ultimately needing a retrace to the April breakout zone (8,000-8,300). Separately, BTIG flags a longer-term quality-factor reversion (quality bottoming vs. a six-year bear market low) even as near-term quality names look vulnerable to unwind. Tactically, BTIG calls XLV's record extension above its 200 DMA a compelling short, AAPL vulnerable both to further risk-off and to any semis/AI bounce, and notes GDX strength diverging from a weak spot gold price.
